title: SLA-prioritized-pacing-and-leaky-bucket-batcher-tuning
author: Asha Gupta
description:
Motivation: Several customers running multi-tenant workloads hit bursts where a small subset of long-context KV-heavy requests flooded continuous batches and caused 99th percentile latency regressions for latency-sensitive SLAs. This PR introduces an SLA-aware pacing layer plus a leaky-bucket admission policy to the continuous batcher to prevent starvation and reduce tail latency without sacrificing throughput. Changes are conservative by default and gated behind a runtime feature flag.

Summary of changes: 1) SLA-prioritized pacing: a lightweight token-based pacing layer that maintains per-tenant and per-route pacing tokens derived from configured SLO weights. Pacing prevents the batcher from immediately accepting large KV-bound requests when tokens are exhausted and instead schedules them into a deferred queue with backoff. 2) Leaky-bucket admission for large requests: requests that exceed a configurable kv-pin-threshold are admitted through a leaky-bucket with capacity and refill tuned to historical per-tenant consumption. 3) Aging-based fairness quantum: if a request remains in queue beyond aging_threshold_ms, it is boosted by a fairness quantum that slowly increases its admission probability to avoid starvation. 4) KV cache pin tolerance: minor change to cache manager to allow ephemeral unpin windows for batched probes so that very short-lived pins do not block eviction under pressure. 5) Backpressure and timeout coordination: a coordinated timeout policy that ties batch admission backoff to request soft timeouts; when KV probes consistently hit long tails the pacing backoff is increased. 6) Observability and dashboards: new SLO-focused metrics and per-tenant pacing counters, and alert rules for pacing saturation. 7) E2E perf harness: added a targeted perf scenario to perf-lab that simulates mixed short+kv-heavy traffic and validates median/95/99 improvements.

Why this is safe: All behavioral changes are feature-flagged and default to off. The pacing and leaky-bucket layers are implemented as admission filters upstream of the existing scheduler; they do not change the core execution path for admitted batches. KV cache unpin windows are time-limited and accompanied by an optional aggressive-evict flag.

Config knobs (defaults included): - batcher.sla_pacing.enabled = false - batcher.sla_pacing.per_tenant_weight = {} (empty => uniform) - batcher.leaky_bucket.enabled = false - batcher.leaky_bucket.capacity_ms = 200 - batcher.leaky_bucket.refill_ms = 50 - batcher.kv_pin_threshold_bytes = 128000 - batcher.aging_threshold_ms = 120 - batcher.backoff.max_ms = 1200

Testing: Unit tests for admission logic and fairness boosting; integration tests in runtime/scheduler_test that inject mocked KV latency distributions; perf-lab scenario ran against a dev cluster and shows median unchanged, 95th improved ~12%, 99th improved ~22% for SLA-weighted tenants, with less than 3% throughput regression in extreme KV-heavy synthetic workloads. CI: all unit/integration tests passed, perf job run locally and attached artifacts.

Rollout plan: behind runtime flags rolled to Canary -> Dedicated staging -> gradual ramp across regions with alerting on pacing saturation and 99th latency regressions.

Related: implements parts of ENG-4127 (multi-tenant tail mitigation) and complements ENG-4198 (kv cache eviction tuning).

release_notes:
Improved continuous batcher stability under mixed short/kv workloads: adds SLA-aware pacing and leaky-bucket admission to reduce 99th percentile latency for latency-sensitive tenants. Feature disabled by default; enable via batcher.sla_pacing.enabled=true.

Notes for operators: watch metrics batcher.pacing.tokens_used, batcher.leaky_bucket.saturation, and runtime.batch.admission_defers. Rolling enable recommended with 10% steps and monitoring for pacing saturation.
